why: The student predicts what happens if the do-while becomes a while loop: the output stays the same because 81 >= 70 is true at the start, and the two loops would differ only when i starts below 70. This correctly reasons about changed code and a class of inputs. However, it never gives the actual output for i = 61, which is "61 ".

The while loop is only the changed code the student compares against. The answer gives no separate reasoning about the while loop itself.
